title: Tidy Data (Journal of Statistical Software, vol. 59, issue 10, 2014)
publisher: Hadley Wickham, Journal of Statistical Software
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Definition of tidy data (each variable a column, each observation a row, each type of observational unit a table) and the paper's five common messy-data problems.

title: Data Organization in Spreadsheets (tutorial behind Broman and Woo, The American Statistician 72(1), 2018)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The practical rules: be consistent, YYYY-MM-DD dates, fill every cell, one thing per cell, make it a rectangle, data dictionary, no calculations in raw data, no colour as data, good names, backups, data validation, save as plain text.

title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed), 5.2 Some simple forecasting methods
publisher: Rob J Hyndman and George Athanasopoulos, OTexts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Mean, naive, seasonal naive and drift methods; these are benchmarks, and a new method that cannot beat them is not worth considering.

title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed), 5.8 Evaluating point forecast accuracy
publisher: Rob J Hyndman and George Athanasopoulos, OTexts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Training and test sets (test typically about 20% and at least as long as the horizon); over-fitting; MAE and RMSE; MAPE problems with zero or near-zero values; MASE below 1 beats naive.

title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed), 5.5 Distributional forecasts and prediction intervals
publisher: Rob J Hyndman and George Athanasopoulos, OTexts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Point forecasts are of little value without intervals; 80% and 95% multipliers of 1.28 and 1.96 for normal errors; intervals widen with the horizon.

title: FORECAST.ETS function
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Uses the AAA version of exponential smoothing; seasonality auto-detected by default (max 8,760); up to 30% missing points filled; duplicates averaged by default; constant timeline step; not available in Excel for the web, iOS or Android.

title: What is Power Query?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 30 Sep 2026). Power Query records refreshable steps without modifying the source; steps are written in M; available in Excel for Windows and Mac and Power BI.

title: Unpivot columns
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 10 Jul 2025). Unpivot output is Attribute and Value; Unpivot other columns picks up new columns on refresh; Unpivot only selected columns does not.

title: Combine files overview
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 29 Aug 2025). Combining a folder of same-schema files through a sample-file query; filter the file list; Changed type steps can error when column names change.

title: Using the data profiling tools
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 28 Aug 2025). Column quality, distribution and profile; profiling uses the first 1,000 rows by default and can be switched to the entire data set.

title: Data types in Power Query
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 14 Aug 2026). Type detection inspects the first 200 rows; locale defaults to the operating system's regional settings; change type using locale for day/month dates; verify by extracting day, month and year.

title: Excel specifications and limits
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 1,048,576 rows by 16,384 columns; 15-digit number precision; applies to Excel for Microsoft 365, 2024, 2021, 2019 and 2016.

title: Files you can store in Google Drive
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Google Sheets files hold up to 20 million cells or 100 MB.

title: QUERY function
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Each column should hold one type; in mixed columns the majority type sets the column type and minority values are treated as null.

title: Introduction to Python in Excel
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Python in Excel calculations run in the Microsoft Cloud, need internet access and use Anaconda libraries.

title: Frequently asked questions about Copilot in Excel
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Edit, Plan and Chat modes; Copilot can make mistakes; review and verify everything; avoid it for decisions in finance, legal or medical topics; eligible subscriptions.

title: COPILOT function
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The COPILOT function was a preview only and is no longer available from 14 September 2026; cells return #NAME? on recalculation; use the Copilot in Excel pane instead.

title: Use the AI function in Google Sheets
supports: Opened with WebFetch. AI function sees only the given range; first 350 selected cells per selection; results refresh manually; may suggest inaccurate information; needs an eligible Workspace or Google AI plan.

title: Data Studio returns as new home for Data Cloud assets (11 April 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Looker Studio renamed Data Studio; existing reports move over with no action; free for individual analysis; Data Studio Pro is the paid team edition.

title: The AQuA Book: guidance on producing quality analysis for government (2025 edition)
publisher: GOV.UK (Government Analysis Function and partners; first edition by HM Treasury)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (published 30 Jul 2025). Proportionate assurance; verification versus validation; the assurer independent of the analyst; commissioner, analyst, assurer and approver roles; managing and communicating uncertainty.

title: Reproducible Analytical Pipelines (RAP)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. RAPs are automated analytical processes; minimum standard: minimise manual steps and document any left, peer review, version control, documented code.

title: Same Stats, Different Graphs (Matejka and Fitzmaurice, CHI 2017)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Datasets with identical summary statistics but very different graphs (Datasaurus Dozen); builds on Anscombe's quartet (1973); always visualise data.

title: Simpson's Paradox (revised 6 June 2026)
publisher: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (Jan Sprenger and Naftali Weinberger)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Definition of Simpson's paradox; the Berkeley admissions example from Bickel, Hammel and O'Connell (1975); choosing the split or pooled table depends on the causal model.

title: 5 key things to know about the margin of error in election polls (8 September 2016)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. About 1,067 cases give roughly plus or minus 3 points at 95%; subgroups have larger margins; the margin on a difference is roughly double; other error sources are rarely reported.

title: Ofqual's statistics policies and procedures: rounding policy (updated 17 December 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Figures normally rounded to the nearest 5; values 1 to 4 shown as fewer than 5; totals and percentages calculated from unrounded figures.

title: How do we ensure anonymisation is effective?
supports: Search-confirmed (ico.org.uk blocks automated fetches with HTTP 403): a search result showed this exact page on 7 Nov 2026. Part of the final anonymisation guidance published 28 March 2025, now under review after the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025. Identifiability is a spectrum; the test is what is reasonably likely; use a motivated intruder test.

title: Guidelines 01/2025 on Pseudonymisation (public consultation)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Pseudonymised data remains personal data if it can be attributed to a person using additional information; only version 1 (consultation, Jan to Mar 2025) is listed.

title: EDPB sheds light on anonymisation and web scraping for generative AI (8 July 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Draft anonymisation guidelines for consultation until 30 October 2026; data is anonymous only if a person cannot be identified by means reasonably likely to be used; criteria of singling out, linkage and inference.

title: Guidance Regarding Methods for De-identification of Protected Health Information
publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services
supports: Search-confirmed (fetch blocked with HTTP 403): a search result showed this exact page. The HIPAA Privacy Rule de-identification standard is met by Expert Determination or Safe Harbor.

title: Business population estimates for the UK and regions 2026: statistical release (5 November 2026)
publisher: GOV.UK (Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, as shown on the page)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 5.6 million private-sector businesses at the start of 2026, down 1.8%; 95% confidence interval of plus or minus 109,000; the release cannot confidently say the population fell; official statistics in development.
